title: foot (dorsum, medial and lateral borders, toes)

chart.description: The foot distal to the ankle unrolled round its long axis. u: distance round the foot (cm) from the dorsal midline (the line of the second metatarsal and the second toe), positive towards the lateral (little-toe) side, negative towards the medial (great-toe) side, continuing over each border down the side of the foot to the border of the red and white (plantar) skin. v: distance along the foot (cm) from the dorsum of the second metatarsophalangeal joint, positive proximal (towards the ankle), negative distal (towards the toes). d: depth below the skin (cm). Offsets: 'cranial' is proximal and 'caudal' distal; 'lateral'/'medial' go further round the lateral/medial side, so on the side of the foot they point towards the sole. The ankle and the heel (malleoli, KI3, BL60 and the points round them) are in the knee-leg chart; the sole is the sole chart.

configurations.label: foot relaxed and supported, ankle near neutral

landmarks.label: centre of the front of the ankle crease (between the extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus tendons)
landmarks.palpation: Dorsiflex the foot: the hollow between the two tendons at the ankle crease.

landmarks.label: dorsum of the first metatarsophalangeal joint
dorsum of the second metatarsophalangeal joint
landmarks.palpation: Flex and extend the second toe: the joint line moves under the finger.

dorsum of the fourth metatarsophalangeal joint
dorsum of the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint
medial side of the first metatarsophalangeal joint, at the border of the red and white skin
landmarks.palpation: The bony prominence of the joint on the inner border of the foot, where the dorsal skin meets the plantar skin.

landmarks.label: lateral side of the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint, at the border of the red and white skin
landmarks.palpation: The joint on the outer border of the foot, where the dorsal skin meets the plantar skin.

landmarks.label: margin of the web between the first and second toes
margin of the web between the second and third toes
margin of the web between the third and fourth toes
margin of the web between the fourth and fifth toes
junction of the bases of the first and second metatarsals
landmarks.palpation: Slide proximally between the first and second metatarsals until the finger stops where their bases meet.

landmarks.label: joint between the base of the second metatarsal and the intermediate cuneiform (dorsalis pedis pulse)
landmarks.palpation: Follow the second metatarsal back to the slight step of its joint with the cuneiform; the dorsalis pedis pulse is felt here, lateral to the extensor hallucis longus tendon.

landmarks.label: junction of the bases of the fourth and fifth metatarsals
landmarks.palpation: Slide proximally between the fourth and fifth metatarsals until the finger stops where their bases meet.

landmarks.label: tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal
landmarks.palpation: The bony knob halfway along the outer border of the foot.

landmarks.label: depression below the cuboid, behind the tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal
landmarks.palpation: On the outer border of the foot, just behind the tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal and in front of and below the lateral malleolus: the hollow under the cuboid.

landmarks.label: medial prominence of the base of the first metatarsal (first tarsometatarsal joint)
landmarks.palpation: Follow the first metatarsal back along the inner border of the foot to the bump of its base.

landmarks.label: tuberosity of the navicular
landmarks.palpation: The prominent bony knob on the inner border of the foot, in front of and below the medial malleolus.

description: The foot distal to the ankle. On the dorsum the extensor tendons run to the toes over the extensor digitorum brevis; the dorsalis pedis artery, with the deep fibular nerve beside it, runs from the front of the ankle to the base of the second metatarsal, where its pulse is felt, and dives between the bases of the first and second metatarsals into the sole; the first dorsal metatarsal artery and the terminal branch of the deep fibular nerve continue to the first web. Between the metatarsals lie the dorsal and plantar interossei: a needle passing straight through an interspace reaches the sole. The dorsal venous arch crosses the metatarsals and drains into the marginal veins on each border. On the medial border, abductor hallucis covers the medial plantar vessels and nerve below the navicular and the base of the first metatarsal; on the lateral border, the lateral dorsal cutaneous (sural) nerve and the lateral marginal vein run superficially past the tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal. The toes have little soft tissue over the phalanges.

review.notes: Positions and depths are illustrative approximations of a reference adult written for simulation. They are not measurements or an atlas and are not a guide to safe depths in real patients. Anatomical expert review is required before any teaching use.
